segments: The eighteenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
And they brought him into the city of Caesarea,
and they swore an oath to him,
and seated him upon the throne of Kayqubad his father,
and proclaimed him Sultan.
And there was joy throughout the whole empire.
And he commanded, and the prisoners who were held captive in his domain were released;
and also those who were in Egypt were likewise freed upon the death of him on whose account they had been captured.
And it is said
that the number of those who were relieved from distress reached twelve thousand.
And that new Sultan wished to seize the chieftains of the Khwarazmians,
because he was afraid of them lest they should rebel.
And he seized a certain great chieftain whose name was Qāyir (Gāyir?) Khan.
And when the rest of them heard [this], they fled and went out from the territory of the Romans (Rūm).
And wherever they passed,
they inflicted bitter destruction.
And they came to Melitene,
and they bound Sayf al-Dawla, its subashi.
And they crossed the Euphrates on foot near the fortress of Masara (or Muqra).
And when they reached the border of the fortress of Zayd, beside the borough of Karbezag,
the armies of those regions encountered them,
and were broken before the Khwarazmians;
and the subashi of the fortress of Zayd, whose name was Bayramiz, was killed.
And they also pillaged the district of Shamishat (or Arshamishat).
And from there they went down to the territory of Sibabarak and of Hamamta (the Hot Springs);
and they stayed there about three years,
plundering the lands.
Afterwards they went and submitted to a youth whose name was Malik Nasir, the lord of Aleppo;
and he gave them Edessa, Harran, and the rest of the cities of Mesopotamia,
and the land was ruined by them.
Now that new Sultan, Ghiyath al-Din, sent and took to himself as a wife the daughter of the Queen of the Iberians (Georgians),
and he loved her greatly.
And he gave himself over to youthful folly,
and began to occupy himself with drinking-feasts, banquets, and playing with birds and beasts.
And he left the administration of the kingdom in the hands of his servants,
and each one began to act according to his own will.
And that Iberian queen had come from her country in the manner of Christians,
and with her were a Catholicos, bishops, priests, and a church.
And with her was also her brother,
who was called David the Younger,
who was king of Inner Iberia (Georgia).
And after a little while she denied the faith and became a Muslim.
And that David her brother and that Catholicos were seized,
and they were imprisoned in one of the fortresses,
